obligation: Acquirer notice of suspected card data compromise (contractual)
citation: Merchant agreements with the acquiring bank (fictional term); PCI DSS v4.0.1 Requirement 12.10 (N71-R04)
trigger: Suspected or confirmed compromise of card data on MID-T or MID-F, including a common point of purchase notice from the acquirer or a card brand
deadline: Within 24 hours of suspecting a compromise (merchant agreement term). Clock starts at suspicion, not confirmation
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual, not law

citation: Visa What To Do If Compromised v10.0 (effective 2026-06-25), Section A.1 - card brand rule applied through the acquirer, not law
trigger: Discovery of evidence sufficient to raise a reasonable suspicion of, or to confirm, unauthorized access to Visa account data or a system that handles it
deadline: Within 3 calendar days of that discovery; the entity must ensure the event is reported to Visa (in practice through the acquirer)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - Visa Level 3 merchant

citation: Visa What To Do If Compromised v10.0, Section A.2
trigger: After notifying Visa
deadline: Within 3 calendar days of notifying Visa
applies_at_this_tier: Yes

citation: Visa What To Do If Compromised v10.0, Section A.4
trigger: Discovery of compromised account data, a Visa request, or a determined window of exposure
deadline: Within 3 calendar days; provided through the acquirer or processor
notify: Visa (via the acquirer or the payment partner)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - the payment partner can extract card numbers used in the window of exposure

citation: Visa What To Do If Compromised v10.0, Section A.5
trigger: Visa requires a PCI Forensic Investigator (PFI)
deadline: Initial forensic report within 5 business days after the PFI contract is signed; final report within 10 business days of completing the investigation. The PFI must not have served the company in the past 3 years
notify: Visa and the acquirer (the PFI reports directly to Visa)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if Visa requires it

citation: Mastercard, American Express, and Discover operating rules - applied through the acquirer, not law
trigger: Suspected compromise of those brands' card data
deadline: Per acquirer and brand instructions (not verified here)
notify: Acquirer; card brands through the acquirer
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - follow acquirer instructions; these rules were not verified

trigger: Breach of security of personal information of Florida residents. Personal information includes a name with a card number and any required security code, and an email address with a password for an online account (501.171(1)(g)). A patron export of names, emails, phones, and order history alone is not personal information under this definition
deadline: Without unreasonable delay and no later than 30 days after the determination of a breach or reason to believe a breach occurred (15 more days if good cause is given to the Department in writing within the 30 days, 501.171(3)(a); applies only to this notice to individuals)
notify: Each affected Florida resident, by mail or email
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - expected for skimmed card data with security codes

trigger: A law enforcement agency determines that notice would interfere with a criminal investigation
deadline: Delay for the period the agency specifies in a written request
notify: Hold individual notices; keep the written request
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if requested

trigger: After investigation and consultation with law enforcement, the company reasonably determines the breach has not and will not likely result in identity theft or other financial harm
deadline: Document the determination, keep it 5 years, and give it to the Department of Legal Affairs within 30 days after the determination
applies_at_this_tier: Unlikely for skimmed card data; counsel decides

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: No later than 30 days after the determination of a breach or reason to believe a breach occurred (the 15-day extension does not apply to this notice)
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs (Attorney General)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if 500 or more Florida residents (likely: about 84% of buyers are Floridians)

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time
deadline: Without unreasonable delay
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if more than 1,000

obligation: Third-party agent breach notice to the company (inbound)
trigger: The ticketing vendor, payment partner, MSP, or another third-party agent has a breach of a system it maintains for the company
deadline: No later than 10 days following the agent's determination of the breach; the company then gives the notices above
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - also add a 72-hour contract term at renewal (POL-03 4.10)

obligation: MSP incident notice to the company (contractual)
trigger: The MSP finds an incident affecting the company's computers, network, suite, or its own remote management tool
deadline: None in the current contract; a 24-hour notice term is being added at renewal (P01 R-015)
applies_at_this_tier: Gap - contract amendment due 2026-12-31

citation: State breach notification statutes (all 50 states, DC, PR, USVI; Guam 9 GCA Ch. 48)
trigger: Breach of computerized personal information of state residents (definitions vary by state)
deadline: Varies by state (for example 'without unreasonable delay' or a fixed number of days)
notify: Affected residents; state attorney general or regulator where the state requires it; consumer reporting agencies above state-set counts
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - apply the law of each state where affected patrons live (about 16% of buyers); some states' definitions may cover the patron export even where Florida's does not

trigger: Suspected criminal compromise of card data or account takeover
deadline: As soon as practical (target day 0 to 2)
notify: FBI (IC3) or U.S. Secret Service field office
applies_at_this_tier: Recommended

trigger: Suspected security incident, data theft, or extortion demand
deadline: Per policy: prompt notice through the 24x7 breach hotline, before hiring outside firms; use panel counsel and forensics
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual, not law

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: Considering a ransom or extortion payment (for example a demand to not publish the patron export)
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if a sanctioned party is involved); law enforcement (FBI) or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Only if an extortion demand is made. All U.S. persons. Strict liability for payments to sanctioned parties

trigger: Cybersecurity incident at a Nevada gaming licensee
deadline: Notify the Chair within 24 hours of activating the incident response plan; Initial Cybersecurity Incident Response report within 5 calendar days; written updates every 30 days; investigation report available on request
notify: Chair of the Nevada Gaming Control Board
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company holds no gaming license and operates only in Florida (N71-R01)

trigger: Suspicious activity at a casino or card club
deadline: No later than 30 calendar days after initial detection of facts that may be a basis for filing
applies_at_this_tier: No - not a casino or card club (N71-R03)

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident and ransom payment reports
trigger: Covered cyber incident (reasonable belief) or ransom payment
deadline: Proposed: 72 hours (incident); 24 hours after ransom payment
applies_at_this_tier: NOT YET REQUIRED: final rule not published as of 2026-09-25 (reporting is voluntary until then). Proposed scope: critical infrastructure entities above the SBA size standard, or meeting a sector criterion regardless of size; the company is far below its SBA size standard

obligation: Covered telecommunications equipment or services discovered
trigger: Contractor identifies covered telecommunications equipment or services
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification; further report within 10 business days
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company holds no federal contracts or subcontracts

trigger: Contractor identifies a Kaspersky covered article
deadline: Within 3 business days of identification; further report within 10 business days
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company holds no federal contracts or subcontracts
